# marina-rules

> Point-in-time exchange trading rules as data, with a Python library and command line. For each trading day it
> answers which rule was in force: China A-share price limits (涨跌停 / 涨跌幅限制), stamp duty (印花税), transfer
> fees, commission caps, tick sizes, trading sessions and T+N; CFFEX, SHFE, INE, CZCE and GFEX futures margins,
> price limits and fees; Hong Kong and US equity rules. Every record carries its effective date, the official
> source, a verbatim quote and a content hash. Built for backtest engines and AI agents: a missing rule is an
> error, never a guess. Not related to boat marinas; the project is named after a person.

Use it to: get the price-limit band, limit-up / limit-down price, tick or statutory fee that applied on a past date;
check a backtest's or broker's fill log against the rules of each day (`marina-check`); pre-flight a backtest window
for gaps (`coverage`); cite the exact rule set a result was computed under (`citation`).

It does not contain: prices, constituents, ST or suspension lists, adjustment factors, trading calendars, DCE
futures, crypto. ST status, board and listing date of a security are supplied by the caller.

## Install and ask

- `pip install marina-rules` — the dataset ships inside the package; no network is used at run time.
- `marina-rules` lists the subcommands; `marina-rules skill` prints the usage notes for agents; `marina-rules capabilities`
  prints everything that can be asked, as JSON.
- Python: `import marina_rules as mr`; `mr.rule_at("price_limit_pct", "2020-08-24", "chinext", "XSHE")`;
  `mr.limit_price(10.0, "chinext", "2021-03-01", "XSHE")`; `mr.rules_for(scope, market)`; `mr.scopes()`.
- One decision shape for any language: `marina-rules query <rule> <YYYY-MM-DD> <scope> [market] --context k=v`;
  act only on status `DETERMINED`.
- Dates are `YYYY-MM-DD`; markets are ISO 10383 codes (XSHG, XSHE, BJSE, XHKG, XNYS, XNAS, CCFX, XSGE, XINE, XZCE, GFEX).

## Documents

- [README](https://github.com/David-Marina/marina-rules/blob/main/README.md): what it is, coverage per market, examples
- [README.zh-CN](https://github.com/David-Marina/marina-rules/blob/main/README.zh-CN.md): 中文入门
- [SKILL.md](https://github.com/David-Marina/marina-rules/blob/main/SKILL.md): step-by-step usage for an AI agent, including when to stop
- [capabilities.json](https://github.com/David-Marina/marina-rules/blob/main/capabilities.json): rules, scopes, required context and known gaps, generated from the data
- [docs/SCHEMA.md](https://github.com/David-Marina/marina-rules/blob/main/docs/SCHEMA.md): record schema and the definition of every rule name
- [docs/decision.schema.json](https://github.com/David-Marina/marina-rules/blob/main/docs/decision.schema.json): JSON Schema of a decision
- [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/David-Marina/marina-rules/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md): what changed in each release and what to re-run

- [Rule pages](https://david-marina.github.io/marina-rules/): one page per market, scope and rule, with every record, its sources and quotes; its own llms.txt lists them as Markdown

## Optional

- [conformance vectors](https://github.com/David-Marina/marina-rules/tree/main/conformance): input → expected pairs for checking another implementation
- [data/](https://github.com/David-Marina/marina-rules/tree/main/data): the records as plain YAML, readable from any language
- [errata](https://github.com/David-Marina/marina-rules/tree/main/errata): cases where market data contradicted a rule, with detectors
